topic: The lion and the clever rabbit
outline:
In a green forest lives a big, bossy lion who shouts at everyone.
He tells the animals to bring him a big basket of food every single day.
The tired animals take turns, and one day it is the small rabbit's turn.
The rabbit walks slowly and thinks of a clever plan.
She tells the lion that another lion in the forest says he is the real king.
The angry lion asks to see him, and the rabbit leads him to an old well.
The lion looks in, sees his own face in the water, roars, and splashes into the shallow well.
He climbs out wet and embarrassed, says sorry, and promises never to bully the animals again.
check: Retold gently after the first version was blocked by the topic check: food instead of animals, and the lion only gets wet.

outline:
On a hot summer day, a thirsty crow flies far looking for water.
He sees an earthen pitcher in a courtyard garden.
He flies down happily, but finds only a little water deep at the bottom.
He tries to tip the pitcher and stretches his beak, but cannot reach the water.
He looks around and sees small pebbles scattered nearby.
He has a clever idea and drops the pebbles one by one into the pitcher.
The water slowly rises to the top.
The crow drinks the cool water, feels happy, and flies away.
check: Made gentle: This tale is already gentle with no killing or cruelty. Only softened the crow's suffering from thirst to feeling hot and tired, suitable for ages 3-9.

Chiu and Kau, the sparrow and the crow
outline:
Chiu the sparrow builds a little house of wax, and Kau the crow builds a house of cow dung.
The rain comes and washes Kau's house away.
Wet and cold, Kau knocks on Chiu's door and asks to come in.
Chiu says, wait, I am bathing my baby.
Kau knocks again; Chiu says, wait, I am feeding my baby.
Kau knocks once more; Chiu says, wait, I am putting my baby to sleep.
At last Chiu opens the door and gives Kau a warm place by the stove.
The rain stops, and the two friends share a snack together.
check: Drafted from the common telling; the ending is softened (no burning). Change it to how your family tells it.
